AGENDA
  GLENDALE WATER AND POWER COMMISSION
  VIA TELECONFERENCE ONLY
 Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water and Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast
 live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office.
 Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
 https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If you have any question about
 matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale Water & Power
 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water & Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  APRIL 5, 2021 AT 4:00 PM

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale Water and Power Commission meeting will be
available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

For public comments and questions during the meeting call (818) 937-8100.

MINUTES
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  VIA TELECONFERENCE

  Monday, April 05, 2021, 4:00 PM

Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, social distancing requirements, and health recommendations
from LA County Public Health Department, this meeting was conducted remotely. All GWP Commission
members and staff utilized video conferencing in order to virtually participate in the meeting.

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:00 p.m.

  Present: President Flanigan, Commissioners Jazmadarian, Lall, and Peterson,
  Absent: Commissioner Kedikian

2. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  President Flanigan stated that he attended the City Council briefing and report regarding the
  100% Clean by 2030 Feasibility Study and commended GWP and staff and Ascend Analytics
  for their efforts. Mr. Craig Kuennen, Interim General Manager for GWP (April), thanked
  President Flanigan for his positive feedback and green power and energy efficiency support.

3. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Customer Service Update
  Ms. Tami Vallier, Customer Services Administrator, provided an update relating to specific
  COVID customer protections at the State and local/ GWP level to relieve customers who
  were/are financially affected amidst the COVID situation. Ms. Vallier covered aging
  receivables, revenue for both the Electric and Water Sections, Customer Service metrics,
  and staffing. Ms. Vallier commended GWP Customer Services staff in providing excellent
  service, notwithstanding staff reductions, remote work, and new equipment, online tools,
  and resources. President Flanigan commended Customer Service for providing exceptional
  service. Ms. Vallier addressed the Commissioners' questions and confirmed the GWP
  website information where residents can receive information and apply for assistance and
  other programs.

  b. Legislative Update
  Mr. Steve Nersesyan, Utility Manager/General Business Management, provided information
  relating to the 2021 legislative calendar and summarized the key energy bills and water
  bills. Commissioner Jazmadarian asked what other bills are supported and/or opposed. Mr.
  Nersesyan answered her question.

  c. Electric Reliability Report
  Mr. Dan Scorza, Chief Assistant General Manager - Electric, highlighted key indices that are
  tracked each year, including SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index), SAIDI
  (System Average Interruption Duration Index), and CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption
  Duration Index). Mr. Scorza discussed the Reporting Exclusions (IEEE 1366 Standard) and
  1
   the five-year benchmarks (2015 – 2019) for SAIFI, SAIDI, and CAIDI and compared
  Glendale with neighboring cities (Burbank, Anaheim, Pasadena, and LADWP).

  Mr. Scorza provided an outage summary by cause for 2016-2020 and noted a good portion
  of outages resulted from Mylar balloons. Mr. Scorza mentioned the City’s Mylar Balloon
  Ordinance adopted in October 2020 and described other programs and projects to improve
  reliability; such as the Tree Trimming and 4kV/12kV Conversion Programs; the Cable
  Replacement Project, and the goals to enhance the Transmission and Distribution
  Inspection Program to replace aging equipment.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None.

5. AGENDA FORECAST
  President Flanigan suggested a preliminary budget presentation which will be tentatively put
  on the June 7th Agenda.

6. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Lall
  Seconded by: Commissioner Jazmadarian
  Motion Passed.

The meeting was adjourned at 5:53 p.m.
